title: GPU allocator fragmentation and tail latency field notes
content:
Goal:
Quick personal lab notebook to capture an anomalous tail-latency pattern I keep hitting on multi-tenant nodes. Suspect: allocator fragmentation + async free interactions (cudaMallocAsync / custom arena) when large KV cache churns cause millisecond-scale stalls that show up at P99+. Need reproducible runs and a triage checklist.

Background / hypothesis:
- When serving long-context generation (seq_len 4k+) concurrently with many short chat requests (seq_len 64), we see spikes at P99+ that correlate with peaks in device memory allocation/free activity.
- Hypothesis: fragmented free lists cause a request to hit a slow slow-path (coalescing or fallback allocation) or trigger page migration from host-pinned memory -> GPU which takes ms. Also, preemption (CUDA context switching) + allocator contention might amplify tail.
- Another angle: KV cache objects are often freed in large chunks; if allocator splits or merges asynchronously, it can cause short stop-the-world stalls in the runtime or kernel launch jitter.

Experiment environment:
- Node: g5.12xlarge-ish (A100-like equivalent in lab infra), 8 GPUs, NCCL 2.x, CUDA 12.0.
- Runtime: inference-runtime commit a1b2c3 (local dev), built with CUDA, jemalloc disabled, using internal "gpu_arena_v2" allocator which falls back to cudaMallocAsync when fragmentation high.
- Models: llama-like-13B-8bit-qat (quantized with int8 kernels), batch_size per-request = 1, streaming enabled.
- Load generator: custom harness (loadgen-lite) that can mix arrival patterns. Key flags used: --qps 120, --mix short:0.7,long:0.3 --short-len 64 --long-len 4096 --shuffle 1 --duration 600s
- Traces: libtrace enabled for epoch, and runtime logging (alloc/free, fallback events).

Quick reproduction command notes (local harness):
./loadgen-lite --target localhost:8080 --qps 120 --mix short:0.7,long:0.3 --short-len 64 --long-len 4096 --duration 600 --warmup 60 --dump-trace traces/run-alloc-20241215.log

What I instrumented:
- allocator events: size, timestamp_ns, free-list-coalesce (bool), fallback_to_cudaMallocAsync (bool).
- GC / eviction events for KV cache: object id, size, time to free.
- kernel launch latency distribution for attention layers (measured as kernel_enqueue_ts->kernel_complete_ts).
- per-request wall-clock and internal stages: enqueue->kv-lookup->kernel-run->retrieve.

Sample run raw findings (one representative run):
- Aggregate QPS: 118 (target 120), 70% short, 30% long.
- Latency summary (ms) observed at client side: p50=14.2, p90=28.6, p95=42.3, p99=120.7, p999=210.3
- Notable: step-shaped spikes in p99 coincident with bursts of deallocations from long requests.

Event correlation snippet (timeline, trimmed):
- 00:23:41.102 alloc(256MB) for KVcache[shard-2]
- 00:23:41.104 free(256MB) KVcache[shard-1] -> free-list add (small blocks)
- 00:23:41.105 fallback_to_cudaMallocAsync(size=256MB) -> took 9.2ms
- 00:23:41.115 request-id=abc123 p99 latency 131ms (internal stall during alloc)
- 00:23:43.002 kernel_launch(attn_layer_4) enqueue->complete 6.1ms (normal)
- 00:23:43.305 free(384MB) KVcache[shard-3] -> coalesce started (sync path) -> 4.8ms stall
- 00:23:43.310 request-id=def456 p99 latency 154ms

Observations:
1) Many p99 spikes (>100ms) line up within +/-5ms of a fallback_to_cudaMallocAsync event. The fallback path is expensive (6-12ms) and is executed in-thread.
2) Free-list coalescing (sync) also accounts for 3-8ms pauses. It is deterministic on contiguous large-block frees.
3) Kernel times themselves are stable (attn kernels median ~5-7ms) but queuing delays accumulate behind alloc stalls.
4) The short requests are most affected because they expect rapid turnaround; when a long request frees a big KV, the allocator stalls, and concurrent short requests see long queuing delays.

Quick experiment variations and results (summary):
A) Disable cudaMallocAsync fallback (force larger preallocated arena): p99 reduced from 120.7ms -> 61.5ms, p999 from 210ms -> 92ms. But memory fragmentation eventually causes OOM after extended runs (>=45min) on high churn workloads.
B) Turn on background async-coalesce thread (offloads coalesce work): p99 -> 48.9ms, p999 -> 78ms; no OOM observed in 90m run. CPU utilization + small perf overhead.
C) Aggressive early preallocation of KV cache pool (reserve contiguous chunks per-shard): p99 -> 29.4ms, p999 -> 42ms; but increases idle memory footprint by +22% (bad for multi-tenant packing).
D) Hybrid approach: async-coalesce + small per-shard reserve -> p99 ~ 32ms, memory overhead +8%. Best compromise so far.

Micro-optimizations tried (and quick notes):
- jemalloc / tcmalloc swap: tcmalloc slightly better for small allocs but no impact on GPU allocator stall events (these are CUDA-side).
- Reduce KV free granularity: instead of freeing 256MB at once, free in 16MB chunks -> fragmentation reduced but number of free ops surged; p99 reduced marginally but CPU overhead increased.
- Serialize frees via dedicated frees thread (queue frees) -> smoothed tails but added 1-2ms to normal frees; overall p99 improved for short requests.

Actionable next steps (for later runs / PRs):
- Short-term (low-effort): enable async coalesce thread and measure 12hr soak on mixed workloads. Add telemetry: count fallback_to_cudaMallocAsync events, coalesce-duration histogram.
- Medium-term: add a small per-tenant reserved arena for KV cache allocations (configurable percent), with eviction heuristics. Run packing sims to quantify cost vs latency.
- Long-term: upstream a small change: move fallback_to_cudaMallocAsync to background allocation thread to avoid blocking request worker thread. This will require careful handling: must ensure allocation finishes before kernel launch; may need speculative reservations.

Triage checklist when a customer sees P99 spikes:
- check traces for fallback_to_cudaMallocAsync events (tag: allocator:fallback) in timeframe of spike
- check for large contiguous frees in last 100ms
- check GPU memory utilization and fragmentation metric (free_list_fragmentation ratio)
- if present, try temporary mitigation: restart process with bigger GPU arena env var or route heavy long-context traffic to separate pool

Random notes and heuristics gleaned:
- KV cache churn pattern that tends to hit: many long requests finishing in same time quantum (e.g., end-of-batch alignment) -> coordinated free bursts. Add jitter to long completions can desynchronize frees and helps tails.
- Preemptions from other system processes can expose allocator pathological behaviour; ensure system-level daemons (backups, metrics exporters) are CPU/nicely pinned away.

Raw ASCII timeline heat (rough):
Time(ms) |     0-2 | 2-5 | 5-10 | 10-20 | 20+
p99 freq |   300  |  85 |  32  |   9   |  4
Most p99s fall in 0-2ms minor blips; the 10-20 and 20+ buckets mostly map to allocator fallback/coalesce.

Open questions / experiment ideas to try next week:
- Can we use cudaMemPoolSetAttribute / cudaMallocAsync tuning knobs to reduce fallback latency?
- Is there a cheap per-GPU defragmentation op we can run during low QPS windows? (analogy to GC compaction)
- Better metrics: expose fragmentation ratio (largest_free_block / total_free) in metrics and add alert when < 0.12.

Notes for a brief GitHub PR description (draft):
Title: async coalesce thread + non-blocking cudaMallocAsync fallback
Summary: add a background thread to perform coalescing of freed GPU blocks and move expensive cudaMallocAsync calls off request worker threads. Add metrics for fallback events and coalesce latency.
Goal: reduce p99 / p999 spikes for mixed short/long workloads while keeping memory efficiency.

TODO (me):
- [ ] implement background alloc/fallback prototype (spike branch: allocator/async-fallback)
- [ ] run 24h soak with mixed traffic, record p50/p90/p99/p999 every hour
- [ ] write short runbook for on-call to mitigate (include restart knob and traffic routing)

End of notes.

Small personal aside: this problem feels like "GC" for GPU memory. We need better ergonomics for non-blocking allocation patterns in the runtime.
